figures.finding: It is prohibited to employ a person under fourteen; a young employee (over fourteen and under eighteen) may not work nights or more than seven hours a day, nor in the work the Minister lists as prohibited.

value.night: barred (hours garbled in the copy: "(J:00 P.M. and 6:00 A.M.")

sources.said: It is prohibited to employ a person under the age of fourteen years.
"Young employee" for the purpose of this Proclamation means a person above the age of fourteen and below the age of eighteen years.
A young employee may not be made to work for more than seven hours per day .

figures.finding: Despite the Civil Code, anyone of fourteen or more may enter a contract of employment, but no such contract is enforceable against a person under eighteen where it is found prejudicial to him; otherwise a minor is represented by his guardian in money matters and may not perform juridical acts save where the law provides; no share of earnings is set aside; the rule reaches any employment, writing and directing included.

sources.said: Notwithstanding any provisions in the Ci\'il Code, any person fourteen years of age or older has the capacity 10 enter into a contract of employment.
No contract of eniployment shall be enforceable against a person below the age of eighteen if it is detem1ined to be prejudicial to the interests of that person,

In matters concerning his pecuniary interests and the administration of his property, a minor shall be represented by his guardian. The minor may not perform juridical acts except in the cases provided by law.

figures.finding: The Labour Proclamation makes no exception for performing: a child under fourteen may not be employed in any work, a performer included, and from fourteen the young-employee limits (seven hours a day, no nights) apply to performing as to writing or directing.
